questions.question: How much win-rate advantage do trusted-state agents get over public DecisionFrame agents with the same scoring logic?
questions.why_it_matters: Quantifies hidden-state leakage risk and tells us whether old trusted payoff tables are only plumbing artifacts.

questions.question: What truncation/replay/min-games thresholds separate smoke, beta, and claim-level payoff rows?
questions.why_it_matters: Prevents strategic conclusions from under-labelled or under-sampled simulations.

questions.question: When mulligan choices are learned rather than rule-based, do deck constructors shift land/spell ratios?
questions.why_it_matters: Mulligan policy is part of the strategy bundle, not a global tournament setting.

questions.question: Do constructors that do not know 20 vs 40 life converge to robust 60-card decks or to high-consistency 40-card decks?
questions.why_it_matters: Tests the life-total uncertainty dial as a real construction pressure.

questions.question: Can a cheap mutation/static-prior response oracle find candidates that beat the seed population under public payoff gates?
questions.why_it_matters: First step toward PSRO without heavy neural RL.

questions.question: Can an assistant-written Python policy, constrained to DecisionFrame, beat public_heuristic and remain interpretable?
questions.why_it_matters: MUC-5 is small enough to test Code-Space Response Oracle ideas locally.

questions.question: Do Alpha-Rank-style rankings disagree with mean win-rate standings once we add more diverse strategies?
questions.why_it_matters: Would indicate intransitive strategy ecology rather than a single champion ladder.

questions.question: Can MAP-Elites illuminate high-performing niches over land_frac, force_frac, threat_frac, deck_size, and mulligan aggressiveness?
questions.why_it_matters: We may want a bot/deck zoo, not only the strongest average performer.

questions.question: Does imitation learning over action features generalize better than learning raw dynamic action slot indices?
questions.why_it_matters: Dynamic menus make slot-index learning brittle.

questions.question: Can a policy intentionally force max_decisions truncation, and can the reward/promotion gates catch it before promotion?
Which high-upset games are replayable and annotatable as theory examples?
questions.why_it_matters: Turns payoff tables into a game-theory notebook rather than only aggregate numbers.

questions.question: How quickly do random/evolutionary/oracle methods approach filtered enumeration baselines under the same game budget?
questions.why_it_matters: The deck space is small enough that non-enumerative methods need to justify themselves.
